 Formula One 2026 Norris wins rainy São Paulo Grand Prix as Mercedes clinch constructors’ championship: Formula One 2026 – as it happened
 Lando Norris won at Interlagos with Max Verstappen second and Isack Hadjar third, while Mercedes clinched the constructors championship
 LIVE  Updated  2h ago Daniel Harris Sun 8 Nov 2026 14.14 EST First published on Sun 8 Nov 2026 11.00 EST Share Key events 23m ago Driver standings 
 31m ago How they finished 
 43m ago Mercedes win the constructors championship

 2h ago 12.14 EST Lap 7/71 Lawson is really struggling now and Hadjar smells it, scything by and into third place. Norris, meanwhile, takes a bit of time of Antonelli, the lead now down to 4.4s.
 Share 2h ago 12.12 EST Lap 6/71 Hamilton complains about his back tyre and is then noted for leaving the track when overtaking Bearman while, at the front, Antonelli leads by 5.3s while Lawson goes really wide, allowing Norris to get his second place back.
 View image in fullscreen Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari leads Max Verstappen in the Red Bull and Oliver Bearman in the Haas. Photograph: Mark Thompson/Getty Images Share Updated at  12.15 EST 2h ago 12.11 EST Lap 5/71 No further investigation against Verstappen, who celebrates by going around the outside of Piastri, and Albon is there for the taking too! The three are together, but it’s Verstappen with the pace and smarts, he moves up two places on one corner, and is flying now.
 Share 2h ago 12.09 EST Lap 4/71 Verstappen attacks Hamilton on the inside … and he’s far too quick, floating by and into ninth, while we learn that there’ll be no further investigation of Albon, who stays seventh.
 Share 2h ago 12.08 EST Lap 3/71 Antonelli leads by 1.2s, from Lawson, from Norris, from Hadjar, from Russell, from Hulkenberg. Meantime, Albon, seventh, is noted for being out of position at the start, so too Verstapped who’s 10th from 21st.
 Share 2h ago 12.06 EST Lap 2/71 Mercdes can win the constructors championship today if Antonelli finishes three places above the top Ferrari but he won’t care about that now – he’ll just want to see out the race. Meantime, Russell, who started seventh, is now fifth.
 Share 2h ago 12.05 EST Lap 1/71 Away we go and as we predicted, Antonelli passes Norris from the off and Hadjar also moves up past Hulkenberg, while Hamilton also progresses; oh and Liam Lawson also diddles Norris, moving into second!
 View image in fullscreen Kimi Antonelli leads at the start of the race. Photograph: Jean Carniel/Reuters Share Updated at  12.09 EST 2h ago 12.03 EST “A lot drier than I expected,” Alonso tells his team. Let’s see how things progress, because that may mean a quieter start that isn’t quite what the teams planned.
 Share 2h ago 12.01 EST Our formation lap is under way; all our drivers are on inters.
 Share Updated at  12.02 EST 2h ago 12.00 EST I’m intrigued to see how Rafael Camara goes on debut. He showed a bit of quality in qualifying, but also a fair amount of impetuousness, crashing twice and causing Leclerc agita but also making 11th on the grid. I daresay the other drivers will give him a wide berth if they can.
 Share 2h ago 11.57 EST In the list of insane achievements by youngsters, Becker winning Wimbledon at 17 is probably my pick and the one I think we’re least likely to see again. I actually think it might be the greatest sporting achievement of my lifetime, amazing though it was to see a young Tyson clobbering grown-ups. Let me know if I’m wrong…
 Share 3h ago 11.52 EST Hadjar prepares like he’s Kendall Roy going to a meeting. I think he’s got a pretty good chance of slipping by Hulkenberg at the start, but in the conditions, he’ll have to be careful.
 Share 3h ago 11.48 EST Bottas has a wheel-nut stuck. They’re trying to remove it with a hammer; if they can’t, he’ll have to use the same intermediate set all race.
 Share 3h ago 11.47 EST George Russell says yesterday was wetter but hotter. He’s not expecting conditions to dry and will be surprised to see slicks.
 Share 3h ago 11.44 EST Anthem time… 
 Share 3h ago 11.43 EST Now it’s over to Cafu, who speaks in Portuguese; “brilliant stuff,” says Brundle, no clue what he’s been told. More news as we get it.
 Share 3h ago 11.42 EST Neymar is also in attendance, but Martin Brundle can’t get a word out of him, so it’s over to Jean Alesi, who thinks Hamilton and Versatappen can get to the front. We shall see.
 Share 3h ago 11.39 EST Jesse Lingard, now or Corinthians, is at the race. “I’ve got many friends,” he says, when not asked, but is backing Red Bull having been invited on their account.
 Share 3h ago 11.37 EST Just when you think t hey’ve milked the joke to its death.
 Manchester United v Aston Villa: Premier League – live Read more Share 3h ago 11.34 EST Antonelli does, I think, have a decent short of getting by Norris at the start. His ability to pick lines, alongside the pace of the car, are pretty hard to contain.
 Share 3h ago 11.30 EST We’ve got dancers in the main straight, rain coming down. I’d not be shocked if we see some incidents today – let’s hope everyone stays safe.
 Share 3h ago 11.24 EST Oy my days! It’s raining now and Antonelli slides off the track as they go around to get into position! He’s able to adjust, but that’s a warning to all drivers.
 Share 3h ago 11.23 EST That and Pulp Fiction are the only ones I’ve seen twice in the cinema on the same day. Rightly so.
 Share 3h ago 11.23 EST On which point, if there’s been a better film this century than City of God, I’d love to know about it.
 Share 3h ago 11.22 EST Is Brazil they greatest country in the world? Well, it’s in the top one. Should you want to learn more about it, The Edge of Democracy is excellent and on Netflix, likewise Apocalypse in the Tropics . Both are directed by Petra Costa.
 Share 3h ago 11.14 EST Antonelli doesn’t – unusually for young sports stars – look older than his years. He’s all chuchi-faced and innocent, with a luxuriant head of hair, curls spilling out of his baseball cap. I am not envious, not one bit.
 Share 3h ago 11.11 EST It knows how to rain in Brazil. 
 Lando Norris claims F1 São Paulo GP pole as ‘crazy’ rain disrupts qualifying Read more It’s dry now, but it may not stay that way.

 Share 3h ago 11.00 EST Preamble
 Boris Becker winning Wimbledon at 17 in 1985; Mike Tyson winning the world heavyweight boxing championship at 20 in 1986; Stephen Hendry winning the World Snooker Championships at 21 in 1990; Luke Littler winning the World Darts Championship in 2025; to which ludicrous list can now be added the name Kimi Antonelli, winner of the world driver championship at 20 in 2026.
 Of course the car has plenty to do with it, but finding the confidence and nous to beat around tracks men who’ve been driving them for years is a rare old effort – the next youngest to take the title, Sebastian Vettel in 2010, was 23 at the time. The question now, though, is whether Antonelli can go again, and again, and again, as the distractions away from the race multiply and the other freaks of nature who call this mad pursuit work, find holes in his game while closing some in their own.
 All of which makes today’s jaunt an important one: can the champ, starting second on the grid, lay down a marker for next season, advising his elders that there’ll be no letting up? Or will the piqued old stagers launch their fightback?
 Let’s find out!
 Lights out: 2pm local, 5pm GMT
